name: Massachusetts

agency.name: Massachusetts Attorney General's Office, Fair Labor Division

rates2026.note: Unchanged since January 1, 2023; no scheduled increases

tipped.note: Service rate for workers who serve customers and receive more than $20 a month in tips; tips must bring pay to $15.00

source.quote: Effective January 1, 2023, the minimum wage is $15.00 per hour and the service rate is $6.75 (applied to workers who provide services to customers and who make more than $20 a month in tips).

overtime.note: Time and a half after 40 hours a week.

source.quote: Overtime pay is at least 1.5 × the regular rate of pay for each hour over 40 hours.

sickLeave.capNote: Earn and use up to 40 hours a year; paid for employers with 11 or more employees, unpaid (job-protected) for smaller employers.
sickLeave.employerThreshold: all employers (paid if 11 or more employees)
sickLeave.note: Massachusetts Earned Sick Time law (M.G.L. c. 149, s. 148C).

source.quote: Employers with 11 or more employees must provide paid sick time. Employers with fewer than 11 employees must provide earned sick time, but it does not need to be paid.

familyLeave.name: Massachusetts Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML)
familyLeave.replacement: 80% of the part of individual average weekly wage up to 50% of the state average weekly wage, plus 50% of the part above, up to the maximum
familyLeave.medicalLeave: Up to 20 weeks medical leave, 12 weeks family leave (26 for a covered service member), 26 weeks combined per benefit year

source.quote: For 2026, the state average weekly wage is $1,922.48 and the maximum weekly benefit rate is $1,230.39. For 2027, the maximum weekly benefit rate is $1,284.61.

finalPay.fired: in full on the last day of work
finalPay.quit: on the next regular payday (or the first Saturday after quitting if there is no regular payday)
finalPay.ptoNote: Earned vacation pay counts as wages and must be paid at separation (same day if fired).

source.quote: In most circumstances, if you are fired you should be paid in full on your last day. If you leave your job voluntarily, you must be paid on the next regular payday.

ptoSource.quote: Workers have a right to their wages, including tips, earned vacation pay, promised holiday pay, and earned commissions

breaks.meal: At least 30 minutes if working more than 6 hours in a calendar day

source.quote: Workers have a right to at least a 30-minute meal break if they work more than six hours during a calendar day.

notes.text: PFML maximum weekly benefit rises from $1,230.39 (2026) to $1,284.61 (2027).

source.quote: In 2026, the maximum weekly benefit is $1,230.39. In 2027, the maximum weekly benefit is $1,284.61.

notes.text: Fired employees must be paid in full on their last day, including accrued vacation; Massachusetts treats earned vacation as wages.

source.quote: Workers have a right to their wages, including tips, earned vacation pay, promised holiday pay

notes.text: The $15.00 minimum wage has not changed since 2023; any increase now needs the legislature or a ballot question.

source.quote: Further increases must be approved either by the legislature or by the people via a ballot question.
